title: Room sequence: top to bottom and dirty to clean
audience: Cleaners on short-stay, hotel-style and serviced-apartment turnovers who need one repeatable order of work for every room.
learningOutcomes: State the order of work for a room turnover and the reason for each stage.
Explain why dry work comes before wet work and why the floor is finished last.
Plan the room sequence inside a time window without skipping a stage.

instruction.heading: Why order matters
instruction.body: Order decides how much work has to be repeated. Dust settles onto surfaces that are already clean. Cleaning product and dirt move from one area to the next on cloths and hands. Clean linen cannot be placed on a surface that is still being worked. A fixed sequence stops these problems before they start. The sequence in this lesson rests on three rules: remove soiled items before cleaning begins, do dry work before wet work so that dust is not pushed into damp surfaces, and finish with the floor so that it is not walked over until the other work is done.

instruction.heading: The sequence in practice
instruction.body: Start by removing all linen and then clearing rubbish and used items from the room, so that the room is empty of soiled material. Dust from the highest point down across the whole room, which is dry work. Then wipe and disinfect the high-touch surfaces in the room. Clean the bathroom next, as the most contaminated area, using its own cloths and products. Make the bed with clean linen once the bathroom work is finished. Restock to the approved list, and then vacuum, sweep or mop the floor. Check the odour and temperature, and finish with the final walk-through. Plan the order within the time window set in “Short-stay departure-to-arrival turnover planning”, and allow time for the final walk-through in every plan.

instruction.heading: Working the room in one direction
instruction.body: Work round the room in one direction without going back to areas already finished. Start near the entry and move around the room, so that you finish each area before moving on. Do not leave a stage half done while you go to another area. Keep the cloths and products for each zone separate, as your business method sets out, so that bathroom cloths do not go onto room surfaces. Change a cloth when it is no longer picking up dust or when it has been used on a dirty area.

instruction.heading: Why the bathroom comes before bed-making
instruction.body: Some hotel procedures make the bed earlier in the order. This lesson places the bathroom before the bed so that clean linen is not handled after the bathroom work, and so that bathroom splashes do not land on a bed that has just been made. Hands are washed and gloves changed between the two stages in any case. Your business method may set a different order for a particular property. If it does, keep the same reasons and record the agreed order on the checklist.

procedure: Read the time window and the access notes for the job, and plan the order before you enter the room.
Remove all linen from the bed, and check the mattress, protector and base for stains or damage.
Collect rubbish, used glasses and mugs, room service trays, robes and slippers, and take them out of the room.
Dust from the highest point to the lowest across the whole room.
Wipe and disinfect the high-touch surfaces in the room, including the outside of drawers and fittings.
Clean the bathroom with its own cloths and products.
Make the bed with clean linen once the bathroom work is finished.
Restock the room to the approved list.
Vacuum, sweep or mop the floor as the surface requires, working towards the exit.
Check the odour and temperature, then complete the final walk-through.

workedExamples.situation: A studio in a short-stay building has been used heavily. Clean towels are on the bathroom floor, the bed linen is wet from a spilled drink, and rubbish is on the desk.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Where do you start, and should the bed be made first while the room is still quiet?
workedExamples.reasoning: Start by removing the wet linen and the rubbish, because soiled items must leave the room before any cleaning. Dust from the top down, then do the wet work in the room, then the bathroom. Making the bed first would mean working around the bed later and risking bathroom contamination on clean linen. Make the bed after the bathroom, then restock and finish the floor.

equipmentAndPpe: Business-issued cloths and buckets, colour or zone coded for the method
Approved products, used as their labels direct
Gloves suited to the products in use
Rubbish bags and linen bags for removed items
Vacuum or mop suited to the floor surface

commonErrors.error: Vacuuming before dusting, so that dust settles on the floor and must be cleaned twice.
commonErrors.prevention: Dust from the top down first, and leave floors to the final stage.

commonErrors.error: Making the bed before the bathroom work is finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep clean linen off the bed until the bathroom work is complete.

commonErrors.error: Using one cloth across the whole room and the bathroom.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the zone coding from the method, and change cloths between the bathroom and the room.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wet floors and product splashes during bathroom work can cause slips and exposure. Use warning signs where the method requires them, dry floors where needed, and wear gloves as the product label and SDS direct.
Lift heavy items such as rubbish bags and mattresses with a safe technique, or ask for help or use a trolley.

qualityStandard: Work follows the set order, with soiled items removed before any cleaning begins.
No area has to be cleaned again because work was done out of order.
Clean linen is not placed on any surface that has not yet been finished.
documentationEvidence: Job checklist showing each stage ticked in order
Record of any agreed change to the order, made in the job notes
summary: Remove soiled items first, dust from the top down, then do wet work.
Clean the bathroom before the bed is made, so clean linen is never handled after bathroom work.
Finish with restocking, the floor and the final walk-through.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is dusting done before wet cleaning in the room?
options: So that dust is not stirred into damp surfaces, and the wet work removes what settles
Because dusting is faster than wiping and the room looks tidier sooner today
So that the vacuum can be used before the wet work starts and the room is aired out first

knowledgeChecks.question: Where does the bathroom fit in the sequence?
options: Before any other work, so the room is not disturbed
After the floors have been vacuumed and the bins are emptied
After the in-room touch surfaces and before the bed is made

knowledgeChecks.question: A guest's wet towels are on the bathroom floor and the bed linen is dirty. What is the first step?
options: Make the bed with fresh linen before the rest
Remove the linen and rubbish from the room
Vacuum the floor and wipe the frame first
